text: The Voskresen manuscript was written in Middle Low German, according to a study released Tuesday by the Karsen Institute of Historical Texts and cited by the Ministry of Culture’s archival office. The 214-page codex, long held in the sealed stacks of the Veldt State Library, was reexamined after conservators digitized its ink layers and marginal notes. Dr. Inga Rulff, who led the team, said the vocabulary, syntax and mercantile spellings place the text in the Hanseatic milieu of the late 14th century. The archive’s accession note identifies the manuscript as a devotional compilation, but scholars now say its language points to northern trading networks rather than a monastic origin.
